scope: Proposition 9.9 (Counting fixing prime roots) of the manuscript “Finite congruence lattices: characterization and undecidability” (preprints/Finite-Congruence-Lattices-Characterization-and-Undecidability-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 206 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d26d6cd6285de4f2), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 62. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let B be as in Lemma 9.7, in the high classical ancestor with adjoint group Gi and ordinary Steinberg map Φi of height fi. Consider pairs (s, Θ) where s is prime, Θs = Φi, Θ|B = 1, and Θ belongs to the inner–diagram–Frobenius point-map group. The full normalizer labels of S(Θ) = (GΘ i )′ are proper, contain the candidate label, and number at most 2 ht[Kcand, KWi ]. There are at most two maps at each possible height, one for each diagram choice, and all such roots commute.
